classification.difficultyReason: Use the symmetric graph to form width times height, differentiate an exponential product and check the derivative's sign before substituting for the maximum area.

content.prompt: The rectangle PQRS has two vertices on the $x$-axis and two on the curve $y=e^{-x^2}$, as shown in the diagram. Find:

spec.description: Symmetric exponential curve with a rectangle beneath it, upper-right vertex P, lower-right Q, lower-left R and upper-left S. Both axes have arrowheads and no numbered ticks. The origin label is omitted under the house graph convention.
spec.mathematics: The curve is y=exp(-x^2). The illustrative rectangle has upper corners at opposite horizontal coordinates and equal positive heights; its width is 2x and height exp(-x^2). The illustrative coordinate used to draw it is not a given.
spec.answerVisibility: All givens and vertex labels remain visible in the question edition. No optimum is marked. Light blue shading identifies the assessed area, replacing source grey under the standard palette; source image hash 6e17ccf8b15ca2c8bbb1ae8c0f1c8a4e38cedd1d97f3526092e3ee66ba877dee.

children.label: a
children.prompt: the value of $x$ for which the rectangle has a maximum area

answer.worked:
The curve is even, so $S=(-x,e^{-x^2})$. Since P is the upper-right vertex, $x>0$.

Width $=2x$ and height $=e^{-x^2}$.
$$\begin{align*}A(x)&=2xe^{-x^2}\\A'(x)&=2e^{-x^2}-4x^2e^{-x^2}\\A'(x)&=2e^{-x^2}(1-2x^2).\end{align*}$$
For a stationary point, $e^{-x^2}>0$, so
$$\begin{align*}1-2x^2&=0\\x^2&=\frac12\\x&=\frac{1}{\sqrt2}\qquad(x>0).\end{align*}$$
For $0<x<\frac{1}{\sqrt2}$, $A'(x)>0$; for $x>\frac{1}{\sqrt2}$, $A'(x)<0$. Thus the area increases then decreases throughout its domain, giving a global maximum at $x=\frac{\sqrt2}{2}$.

children.label: b
children.prompt: the maximum area of the rectangle.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}A\left(\frac{\sqrt2}{2}\right)&=2\left(\frac{\sqrt2}{2}\right)e^{-(\sqrt2/2)^2}\\A\left(\frac{\sqrt2}{2}\right)&=\sqrt2\,e^{-1/2}\\A\left(\frac{\sqrt2}{2}\right)&=\sqrt{\frac2e}.\end{align*}$$
The maximum area is $\sqrt{\frac{2}{e}}$ square units.
